Subject: Re: Request: AWS private offer — invoicing cadence & term options (Acme Health)

Hi Maria — thanks, and great to hear you enjoyed the demo. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) Term length: We can do a 12-month private offer on AWS Marketplace. Common configuration is a 12-mo commitment with pro-rated activation for mid-cycle starts. Renewal can be set to opt-in (off by default) — we’ll include that in the offer metadata.

2) Invoicing & payment terms: Marketplace private offers typically settle through the marketplace flow, which often results in a marketplace invoice cadence (AWS payouts to sellers). For enterprise customers that require net-45 and a single annual invoice to a specific legal entity, we have two approaches: 
  - Option A (recommended): Create the private offer on AWS and then route a Redwood-issued invoice (seller-side) to Acme with net-45 terms — we accommodate this for enterprise deals. This preserves marketplace activation while meeting your payment terms.
  - Option B: If finance/legal at Acme cannot accept marketplace routing, we can do a direct purchase (outside Marketplace) using a Redwood enterprise invoice and contract. That is operationally heavier.

3) Buyer evidence: I’ve attached a ZIP with the typical evidence bundle we provide for Marketplace purchases (SOC 2 summary, IR contact, IP allowlist instructions, audit log export sample). See attachment: redwood-marketplace-evidence.zip. Our security team can also produce a short intake checklist for your security reviewer.

Next steps I recommend: 
- Confirm which billing entity to name on the PO (Acme Health Systems v. Acme Health US).
- Confirm you want us to proceed with Option A (private offer + Redwood invoice net-45). If yes, I’ll open the private offer and attach the DocuSign order form for signature.

I’m copying Vanessa (marketplace ops) and Vivek (finance) to confirm internal gating items.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Hi Maria — looping in a couple of operational notes so your procurement/finance can triage quickly: 

- Finance gating: For Redwood to issue a net-45 seller invoice tied to a private offer we need: final legal name, remit-to address, tax ID (W-9/EU equivalent), and a signed order form. PO number is fine to capture in the DocuSign form.
- Security gating: SOC 2 Type II summary is fine as a first pass; if your sec team needs tests of controls evidence we can coordinate a short call.
- Buyer approval lanes (what will block activation): Procurement sign-off, Security acknowledgement (we mark as "accepted" in our activation checklist), and Finance clearance for net-45. If any of these are delayed we can provision a 14-day activation buffer before enforcing usage limits.

Attached: po_template.pdf, finance-gating-checklist.xlsx

If you confirm the billing entity and that Acme will accept Redwood invoices with net-45, we’ll generate the private offer and the DocuSign order with the 12-mo term and opt-in renewal set to off.

Thanks — Vanessa
Director, Marketplace Operations
Redwood Inference
